weather.instructions: Read this as a wish for the miniature town. Rain, drizzle or snow arriving in the proposed scene, even poetically and alongside residents reacting, means rain or snow. Imperative wording is unnecessary. Asking rain/snow to end means clear. Only a future condition (after rain stops), past recollection, hypothetical question or explicit keep-as-is means keep; do not implement a condition immediately.

scope:weather.instructions: Does this wish describe desired rain, drizzle, snow or cessation? Direct statements and poetic scene descriptions count as yes, even with other clauses about residents reacting. No imperative verb is needed. Only mentioning weather as a future condition, past memory, hypothetical question, or explicitly keeping it unchanged means no. Interpret figurative weather as yes when it is the requested scene, but not a mere comparison of emotions.

mood_intent.instructions: User speaks to an artistic miniature town. Present feelings, sensory impressions, loose associations and poetic fragments are soft invitations, even without imperative verbs or a request to change the town. Interpret generously when there is any meaningful emotional link. A current personal feeling is enough; do not demand a named action. Emotion transformed into imagery is a metaphor, not a demand to manufacture its imaginary objects. Pure praise of the interface or a completed event, hypothetical questions, and explicit keep-as-is are not invitations. A memory used to evoke a feeling now can be an invitation. Personal needs such as hunger or wanting company are mood invitations, not literal object manipulation. A wish to hear human voices evokes social company; it does not require new speech synthesis. Choose literal if a concrete supported activity/time/weather/person/object is the meaning of the wish; poetic adjectives alone do not make it mixed. Choose mixed for a concrete request PLUS a separately desired town-wide feeling. Choose mood for a feeling or evocative metaphor without a concrete supported command.

criteria.literal: A specific action, communal activity, time, weather or object request, including poetic phrasing
criteria.mixed: Both specific actions AND an independent invitation for the whole town to evoke a mood
criteria.no_change: Only praise, memory, hypothetical or explicit leave unchanged

weather.instructions: Read this as a wish for the miniature town. Rain, drizzle or snow arriving in the proposed scene, even poetically and alongside residents reacting, means rain or snow. Imperative wording is unnecessary. Asking rain/snow to end means clear. Only a future condition (after rain stops), past recollection, hypothetical question or explicit keep-as-is means keep; do not implement a condition immediately.

scope:weather.instructions: Does this wish describe desired rain, drizzle, snow or cessation? Direct statements and poetic scene descriptions count as yes, even with other clauses about residents reacting. No imperative verb is needed. Only mentioning weather as a future condition, past memory, hypothetical question, or explicitly keeping it unchanged means no. Interpret figurative weather as yes when it is the requested scene, but not a mere comparison of emotions.

mood_intent.instructions: User speaks to an artistic miniature town. Present feelings, sensory impressions, loose associations and poetic fragments are soft invitations, even without imperative verbs or a request to change the town. Interpret generously when there is any meaningful emotional link. A current personal feeling is enough; do not demand a named action. Emotion transformed into imagery is a metaphor, not a demand to manufacture its imaginary objects. Pure praise of the interface or a completed event, hypothetical questions, and explicit keep-as-is are not invitations. A memory used to evoke a feeling now can be an invitation. Personal needs such as hunger or wanting company are mood invitations, not literal object manipulation. A wish to hear human voices evokes social company; it does not require new speech synthesis. Choose literal if a concrete supported activity/time/weather/person/object is the meaning of the wish; poetic adjectives alone do not make it mixed. Choose mixed for a concrete request PLUS a separately desired town-wide feeling. Choose mood for a feeling or evocative metaphor without a concrete supported command.

criteria.literal: A specific action, communal activity, time, weather or object request, including poetic phrasing
criteria.mixed: Both specific actions AND an independent invitation for the whole town to evoke a mood
criteria.no_change: Only praise, memory, hypothetical or explicit leave unchanged
criteria.unclear: No coherent direction can be inferred

atmosphere.instructions: Choose ONE artistic interpretation of the feeling the speaker wants the town to evoke. You may interpret poetic imagery. weather.instructions: Read this as a wish for the miniature town. Rain, drizzle or snow arriving in the proposed scene, even poetically and alongside residents reacting, means rain or snow. Imperative wording is unnecessary. Asking rain/snow to end means clear. Only a future condition (after rain stops), past recollection, hypothetical question or explicit keep-as-is means keep; do not implement a condition immediately.

scope:weather.instructions: Does this wish describe desired rain, drizzle, snow or cessation? Direct statements and poetic scene descriptions count as yes, even with other clauses about residents reacting. No imperative verb is needed. Only mentioning weather as a future condition, past memory, hypothetical question, or explicitly keeping it unchanged means no. Interpret figurative weather as yes when it is the requested scene, but not a mere comparison of emotions.

mood_intent.instructions: User speaks to an artistic miniature town. Present feelings, sensory impressions, loose associations and poetic fragments are soft invitations, even without imperative verbs or a request to change the town. Interpret generously when there is any meaningful emotional link. A current personal feeling is enough; do not demand a named action. Emotion transformed into imagery is a metaphor, not a demand to manufacture its imaginary objects. Pure praise of the interface or a completed event, hypothetical questions, and explicit keep-as-is are not invitations. A memory used to evoke a feeling now can be an invitation. Personal needs such as hunger or wanting company are mood invitations, not literal object manipulation. A wish to hear human voices evokes social company; it does not require new speech synthesis. Choose literal if a concrete supported activity/time/weather/person/object is the meaning of the wish; poetic adjectives alone do not make it mixed. Choose mixed for a concrete request PLUS a separately desired town-wide feeling. Choose mood for a feeling or evocative metaphor without a concrete supported command.

criteria.mood: An implied or explicit invitation to evoke an atmosphere
criteria.literal: A specific action, communal activity, time, weather or object request, including poetic phrasing
criteria.mixed: Both specific actions AND an independent invitation for the whole town to evoke a mood
criteria.no_change: Only praise, memory, hypothetical or explicit leave unchanged
criteria.unclear: No coherent direction can be inferred

atmosphere.instructions: Choose ONE artistic interpretation of the feeling the speaker wants the town to evoke. You may interpret poetic imagery. Do not invent objects, people or new physical capabilities. This is a mood choice, not an exact-command detector. Use the closest feeling for a meaningful present sensory or emotional fragment. Use keep only for interface praise, purely retrospective event comments, hypothetical questions or explicit keep-as-is. Loneliness suggests togetherness; fatigue suggests rest; food aromas or hunger suggest a warm meal.

criteria.together: Companionship, reunion, human closeness, less loneliness
criteria.celebration: A little joy, festive surprise or a reason to celebrate
criteria.quiet: Rest, a slow exhale, less bustle, release of tiredness
criteria.hopeful: Freshness, hope, a new beginning, a touch of spring
criteria.hearth: Hunger, food aromas, warm meals, the comfort of a kitchen
criteria.drizzle: Soft rain, damp evening air, raindrops on eaves
criteria.snowfall: Winter, falling snow, soft white flakes; not emotional loneliness
